title: Is Your Explanation Reliable: Confidence-Aware Explanation on Graph Neural Networks

problem.claim: The reliability of post-hoc instance-level explanations for GNN predictions is uncertain, particularly on out-of-distribution or unknown test datasets.

gap.claim: Existing GNN explanation methods do not adequately quantify the reliability of their generated explanations.

contributions.claim: The paper introduces ConfExplainer, an explainer framework with a confidence scoring module for GNN explanations.
The framework is grounded in GIB-CC, a generalized graph information bottleneck with confidence constraint.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that experimental results demonstrate the superiority of their approach.
The authors report that the confidence score enhances the trustworthiness and robustness of GNN explanations.

narrative_sequence.summary: GNN explanations are important for interpreting black-box model behavior and extracting insights from predictions.
The reliability of existing post-hoc instance-level explanations remains uncertain, especially on unfamiliar test data.
ConfExplainer addresses the challenge by adding confidence scoring based on GIB-CC to quantify explanation reliability.
Experiments are reported to show superior performance and improved trustworthiness and robustness of explanations.

source_observation.claim: Explanation methods may need an explicit confidence score when applied to out-of-distribution or unknown data.

interpretation.claim: Reliability assessment can be treated as a distinct component of explanation generation rather than assumed from the explanation alone.

application.claim: For graph-based model explanations, consider attaching calibrated confidence or reliability estimates to generated explanations.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach generalizes beyond the reported GNN settings or datasets.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the evaluated datasets, baselines, metrics, or numerical results.
The abstract does not describe the theoretical guarantees or implementation details of GIB-CC and ConfExplainer.
